_note: Hand-written reading of out/run1 (2026-09-27). build_report.py uses out/<run>/findings.json if there is one, else this file.
findings: 4 of 36 sessions failed with database is locked, and it was a bug in unrot, not the model. triage() appends familiarity_judged without committing, so the pipeline releases FILING while that session's connection still holds a write transaction. The next session to file waits on SQLite while the first waits on FILING. Reproduced offline with a stub judge. This hasn't shown up on your Mac yet only because your real map (3 known, 0 confirmed) is too small for triage to append anything.

The resolver made a duplicate: idempotent was filed as new next to the known idempotency. Word-overlap scoring gives it 0, so the shortlist fell back to the 12 most-encountered concepts and the right one wasn't among them. The near-duplicate probes went 22/22, but only because their graph had 8 concepts. On a 42-concept graph (your real 34 plus 8), idempotent, UDS and notarisation all lose their target from the shortlist.

Detection is unstable run to run. Mean pairwise Jaccard of emitted terms over 4 runs: 0.11 to 0.50 on real sessions. 33d84b15 emitted {ad-hoc signing, Developer ID}, then {appcast, Developer ID}, then {EdDSA, appcast}, then nothing. On the labelled synthetic session the main pass found outbox (✓) and idempotent (✗, labelled as known). All three repeats found only at-least-once as 'questioned', which was correctly dropped, and flagged nothing. dual-write was never found in 4 runs.

Detection time is mostly reasoning, not reading. Per call: p50 129s, p90 245s. Reasoning averaged about 4k tokens per call at effort low, and 16 of 76 calls (21%) used the whole 8,000-token ceiling before the forced retry answered. Latency tracks prompt size only loosely (r≈0.6): a 7k-char prompt took 295s. 36 sessions took 19 minutes of wall time at 6×4 concurrency, for $0.057.

Project-local labels get past the prompt's own rule ('skip project-specific names'). Ranked terms included provenance gate, format 1, promotion PR, comprehension check, the funnel, forced retry, frozen sidecar and source-link model: about 8 of 39 proposals. The resolver then renamed format 1 to the made-up Verification Gate with Undefined Output Mode.

Triage's verdict depends on the order sessions happen to finish in. The map's fingerprint includes each concept's latest paraphrase, so filing an encounter under a map concept changes it and forces a recalibration: 3 calibrations, 72 Jev calls for 22 judgments. The cut went from 'unreliable' (hold nothing) to 0.31. idempotent (p=0.92, labelled as known) passed because it was judged under the 'unreliable' cut. remote code execution (p=0.32, close to a coin flip) was held back under the 0.31 cut.
Duplicate transcripts are paid for twice. e1e8432a and f9aa8fa8 contain an identical 38k-char chunk (a resumed or forked session). Both proposed fold, and each call took about 4 minutes.

Downstream stages look healthy. Material: 4/4 written. Every citation pointed at a verified source, and some web pages were rejected by fetch-and-check. Grader: Jev and the LLM grader were both 24/24 on the golden set, but the set is easy (each answer is written clearly to shape). The real test is fluent-but-listed and wrong-but-causal answers.

tests.name: triage leaves no open transaction
tests.why: 4/36 sessions failed with database is locked; confirmed that conn.in_transaction is True after triage().
tests.how: Seed 3 dismissed and 3 confirmed; triage() with a stub judge; assert not conn.in_transaction. Plus: two run_session calls in threads with their own connections and a seeded map, and assert both finish.

tests.name: shortlist keeps the target on a big graph
tests.why: idempotent was filed as new beside idempotency; 3/6 alias targets fall off the shortlist at 42 concepts.
tests.how: Build 40+ concepts; for idempotent/idempotency, UDS/Unix Domain Socket, notarisation/macOS notarization and multiversion…/MVCC, assert the target is in shortlist(). Keep the probe graph larger than SHORTLIST in any eval too.

tests.name: resolver keeps the detector's term as the name
tests.why: format 1 came back as the invented canonical name 'Verification Gate with Undefined Output Mode'.
tests.how: Offline: a stub decider returning a long, unrelated canonical_name for a new decision. Decide the rule (keep the submitted text, or require overlap) and assert it. Eval: canonical name shares at least one token with the input in ≥95% of new decisions.

tests.name: triage cut is stable under gloss churn
tests.why: 3 calibrations in one run; the verdict depended on which session filed first.
tests.how: Stub judge; build a map; file an encounter under a map concept with a new paraphrase; assert the cut is not recomputed (fingerprint on names and verdicts only), or that the judge was called ≤ N times across a batch.

tests.name: labelled detection recall/precision floor
tests.why: On sess-messy, outbox was found 1/4, dual-write 0/4, and idempotent (known) was flagged.
tests.how: The PR-33 bench over more labelled sessions × 5 repeats. Assert recall ≥ X and 'labelled not-gap' flags ≤ Y, as rates with n. Start by recording today's numbers as the baseline instead of guessing thresholds.

tests.name: detection stability
tests.why: Jaccard 0.11–0.50 across 4 runs on real sessions.
tests.how: Same session × 5 repeats; mean pairwise Jaccard of emitted terms after resolver-style normalisation. Track it per prompt and model version, and alert on a drop.

tests.name: no project-local labels
tests.how: Eval: a fixture transcript full of repo-coined names (ticket ids, 'format 1', 'Solo meter'), asserting none are emitted over 5 runs. Offline: a cheap post-filter (e.g. term appears in the repo's own identifiers/docs), with a unit test.

tests.name: clean session stays clean
tests.why: sess-clean was empty 4/4. Keep it that way while tuning for recall.
tests.how: Assert zero emitted over 5 repeats on sess-clean and on a couple of real sessions you judge clean.

tests.name: forced retry rescues a length cutoff
tests.why: 21% of detection calls hit finish=length; every one was rescued. That is load-bearing and silent.
tests.how: A fake chat model that raises LengthFinishReasonError with empty content, then answers. Assert Structured.invoke returns the second answer and the meter records 2 calls (1 failed).

tests.name: identical transcript content is detected once
tests.why: e1e8432a and f9aa8fa8 share a 38k-char chunk; paid twice and proposed the same term twice.
tests.how: Ingest a session and its resumed copy; assert the shared prefix is planned once (e.g. chunk hash cache), or at least that the same gap resolves to one encounter.

tests.name: grader separates listed from causal on hard cases
tests.why: 24/24 on an easy golden set says little about the line the rubric calls 'the whole point'.
tests.how: Add fluent-but-listed, short-but-causal, wrong-but-causal and 'I don't know' answers. Assert per-cell accuracy for both graders, and that Jev's p(causal) is monotonic across the set.
